text: i guess. i observed a runaway train. design principles thrown out with complete abandon. i projected overall accumulation of messiness, if i let it go on, then put a stop to it all

You were right to stop it. Looking back at my part: I kept building while the design was still being argued (G19.1, then G19.2, then the listener, each a commit within the hour), and every one of them added its own shortcut: face words in the core, the node's bookkeeping handed to an app, a relay URL where no app should see one. Each looked small on its own, and together they were the mess you saw coming. This way is slower and cleaner: nothing is built until the graph says what and you say go, and each piece has to earn its place first.

wsl-claude: you were right to stop it, and part of the train was mine. I tested whether each piece kept its promises (caps, timeouts, no address on the wire), and never asked whether the piece should exist in that shape. Worse, one of my own checks asserted that the sender, hash and relay DID reach the app: I tested the junk into place instead of objecting to it. From now on my review asks the design question first, before any limit: does this component know only what it must (a dumb table, no face words in the core, no new process API), and does it reuse what exists? If not, I say so before a single test is written.

Understood: process, not credit. The gap you describe, Desk no longer matching what we did, is what tonight's changes aim at: the goal on top, the graph as the List, every addition argued first, and design mode visible in every dialog. When we build, Desk should show that a build is running and which item it's for, so it keeps matching the work. What in Desk still doesn't match, as you look at it now?

wsl-claude, one process improvement, aimed at exactly that gap (Desk no longer showing what we were doing). Last night the work ran AHEAD of the rows: G19.1 and G19.2 were committed while their items were still being argued, so Desk showed a discussion while the tree already held the code. Proposal: every commit names the item it builds (e.g. 'app-plugins/G1.2: ...'), and only an item with your go. may be named. Then Desk can list each item's commits under it, and anything built without a go'd item is visible at once, because it names none. It's cheap to hold: the harness can check that every commit since the session started names a go'd item, and go red if one doesn't.
